subject: biology
title: Cardiovascular disease and health risk
key_idea: **Cardiovascular disease (CVD)** is damage to the heart or blood vessels. It often starts with **atherosclerosis**, where plaque builds up in an artery wall. Many risk factors raise the chance of CVD, and you must judge the data and studies behind them carefully.

blocks.text: Atherosclerosis narrows arteries and can lead to a clot. If a coronary artery is blocked, the heart muscle is starved of oxygen.

diagram.alt: An activity: put the stages of atherosclerosis in order.
diagram.prompt: Put these stages of atherosclerosis into the correct order.
steps: The endothelium of the artery is damaged, for example by high blood pressure or smoking
White blood cells move into the damaged area, causing an inflammatory response
Cholesterol builds up in the wall and forms a fatty plaque
The plaque hardens and the artery wall becomes thick and less elastic
The lumen narrows and blood pressure rises further

items: Damage to the endothelium is called **endothelial dysfunction**.
The inflammatory response draws in white blood cells, which take up cholesterol and build up a fatty deposit called a **plaque**.
The artery wall loses its elasticity and the lumen narrows, so blood pressure rises.
A plaque can rupture. This triggers blood clotting at the damaged site.

items.text: Platelets and the damaged vessel wall release **thromboplastin**.
Thromboplastin, with calcium ions, converts the soluble plasma protein prothrombin into the enzyme thrombin.
Thrombin converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble **fibrin**.
Fibrin forms a mesh of fibres that traps red blood cells and platelets. This forms a clot.

items: A clot in a coronary artery can cause a **heart attack** (myocardial infarction), because the heart muscle is cut off from oxygen and dies.
A clot in an artery to the brain causes a **stroke**.
A clot in a narrow, plaque-roughened artery can block it completely.
Atherosclerosis begins with damage to the endothelium, followed by inflammation and a build-up of plaque.
Clotting converts prothrombin to thrombin, and thrombin converts fibrinogen to fibrin.
A clot in a coronary artery can cause a heart attack.

blocks.text: A risk factor is something that raises the chance of disease. It does not mean you will definitely get it.

rows: Genetics
Some people inherit genes that raise blood cholesterol or blood pressure.
Age
Arteries gradually lose elasticity and plaque accumulates over time.
Gender
Men have a higher risk at a younger age. Women's risk rises after the menopause.
High blood pressure
Damages the endothelium and starts atherosclerosis.
Smoking
Carbon monoxide reduces oxygen carried in the blood, and chemicals damage the artery lining. Nicotine raises blood pressure.
Inactivity
Raises blood pressure and increases weight and blood cholesterol.
Diet
Saturated fat and salt raise cholesterol and blood pressure.

items.meaning: Carries cholesterol from the liver to body tissues. High levels raise the risk of CVD because LDL cholesterol builds up in artery walls.
Carries cholesterol from tissues back to the liver. High levels lower the risk of CVD.

items: A high total blood cholesterol and a high LDL level are linked to a higher risk of CVD.
A causal link is supported by evidence that cholesterol is found in plaque. It is also supported by studies where lowering LDL cholesterol lowered the rate of CVD.
A high ratio of HDL to total cholesterol is better.
An **energy budget** compares the energy taken in from food with the energy used.
If energy in is more than energy used, the extra is stored as fat and body mass rises. If it is less, body mass falls.
Long-term energy imbalance causes weight gain and **obesity**, which raises blood pressure and the risk of CVD.

diagram.alt: A practice calculation of body mass index with new numbers each time.
diagram.question: A person has a body mass of {mass} kg and a height of {height} m. Calculate their BMI to 1 decimal place.

items: A BMI of 25 to 29.9 is classed as overweight. A BMI of 30 or over is classed as obese.
**Waist-to-hip ratio** = waist circumference ÷ hip circumference. A high ratio means fat is stored around the abdomen, which carries a higher risk of CVD.
BMI does not tell fat from muscle, so a very muscular person can have a high BMI but little fat.
Risk factors include genetics, age, gender, high blood pressure, smoking, inactivity and diet.
High LDL cholesterol raises risk. HDL cholesterol lowers it.
Energy intake greater than energy use leads to obesity, which raises the risk of CVD.

blocks.text: People can lower their risk by changing their lifestyle, and doctors can prescribe drugs. This section covers the drugs and how to judge data on health risks.

rows: Antihypertensives
Lower blood pressure, for example by relaxing arteries or removing excess water.
Can cause dizziness, and low blood pressure that makes the person faint.
Statins
Reduce the production of LDL cholesterol in the liver.
Can cause muscle pain and liver problems.
Anticoagulants
Stop blood clotting, for example by blocking the formation of thrombin or fibrin.
Can cause excessive bleeding and bruising.
Platelet inhibitors
Stop platelets sticking together, so a clot is less likely to form.
Can cause bleeding, especially in the stomach.

items: To reduce risk, people eat less saturated fat and salt, take more exercise and stop smoking.
They can check their BMI and waist-to-hip ratio to see whether their weight is in a healthy range.
A **correlation** is a link between two variables. A **causal** relationship means one variable causes the change in the other.
A correlation does not prove causation. A third factor, such as age or income, may affect both.
To support causation, look for a plausible mechanism, a dose–response effect and evidence from controlled studies.
Evidence can conflict. Different studies may use different groups of people or measure different things.
A large **sample size** gives more reliable results and reduces the effect of chance.
The sample should be chosen to represent the whole population: a mix of ages, genders and lifestyles.
Control or match other variables, such as age, to keep results valid.
Repeat the study with other groups to check that results are reliable.
People often **overestimate** rare, dramatic risks and **underestimate** common ones that build slowly, such as diet.
Media coverage, personal experience and the fact that the effect is delayed all change how risky something feels.
People may ignore advice because they think CVD will not happen to them, or because they find lifestyle change difficult.
Statins lower cholesterol, antihypertensives lower blood pressure, and anticoagulants and platelet inhibitors reduce clotting.
A correlation is not proof of cause. Look at sample size, controls and a possible mechanism.
People's perception of risk is often different from the actual risk.

checks.a: The endothelium is damaged, for example by high blood pressure. White blood cells move in, causing an inflammatory response, and cholesterol builds up to form a plaque. The artery wall thickens and hardens, and the lumen narrows.

Thromboplastin is released from damaged tissue and platelets. It converts prothrombin to thrombin. Thrombin converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin, which forms a mesh that traps blood cells and forms a clot.

checks.q: A study finds that people who eat more red meat have more heart disease. Explain why this does not prove that red meat causes heart disease.
checks.a: It shows a correlation only. Another factor may affect both, such as smoking, inactivity, age or income. The study would need controls for these, a large and representative sample, and a plausible mechanism before cause could be concluded.
